Key Insights Apr 2026
🏆
Victoria record spend: $46.7B in 2025, cementing 2nd place nationally. Melbourne remains the #1 interstate overnight leisure destination with 3.5M visitors spending $5.9B.
✈️
Outbound boom: Australians took 12.4M overseas trips in 2025, forecast to surpass 13M in 2026. Average spend is AUD $9,800/trip — 15% above pre-pandemic.
🇯🇵
Japan is the standout: +24.9% YoY growth for Australian outbound travel to Japan. Strong AUD vs Yen driving interest. RACV tour partners actively promoting Japanese itineraries.
⚠️
US travel declining: September showed a -12.7% drop in Australians travelling to the USA. High airfares and cost pressures are redirecting demand to Asia. Watch RACV USA product mix.
🌏
China rebound strong: Chinese visitors to Victoria spent $3.1B, +15.4% YoY. India volume #1 nationally for VIC with $808M spend. Key inbound segments for Melbourne.
🛳️
Cruise & luxury touring up: APT, Viking, Scenic cruises all posting record bookings. RACV member segment aligns strongly with 55+ demographic driving premium travel demand.

Key Destination Trends
🌴
SE Asia dominates 2026 trending list: Vietnam, Malaysia, and the Philippines leading, driven by affordability and strong AUD/local currency rates.
❄️
"Coolcation" trend rising: Nordic/Baltic destinations (Norway, Finland, Estonia) up 20–60% YoY. Off-season Italy bookings up 166% (Intrepid data).
🏝️
Domestic standouts: Hamilton Island (#7 Google) and Lord Howe Island (#9) showing strong domestic intent. RACV resort pipeline opportunity in QLD coastal.

Aviation Developments
✈️
Qantas Project Sunrise (2026): Nonstop Sydney–New York and Sydney–London launching H2 2026. Game-changer for ultra-long-haul leisure bookings.
🍁
Qantas Vancouver–Sydney daily: Launched Jan 2026 (+68% seat increase). North America capacity up substantially — watch for RACV Canada/Alaska tour demand.
📊
Intl. passenger growth +9.5%: August 2025 vs prior year. Jetstar and Qantas top contributors. Singapore Airlines, Emirates holding strong market share.
🏙️
Domestic routes expanding: Adelaide–Melbourne, Gold Coast–Sydney, Brisbane–Melbourne all up 3–6% capacity. Good for RACV resort and domestic tour products.

Facebook / Meta Ads: Cover-More and Allianz run heavy retargeting campaigns post-quote-abandonment. Estimated $500K–$1M+ monthly Meta spend each. Seasonal surges Jan–Feb (summer hols) and Jun–Jul (Europe season). RACV spend relatively light.
📸
Instagram: Cover-More runs destination-linked creative ("Heading to Bali? Get covered"). Allianz leverages UGC and travel influencers. RACV opportunity: tie TI creative to RACV's own destination content and resort imagery.
▶️
YouTube: Allianz runs claims-reassurance ads and destination pre-rolls. Cover-More has branded content series. RACV has minimal YouTube TI presence — opportunity to run pre-roll against travel content (Japan, Bali, Europe searches).
🔍
Comparison Sites (Finder, Canstar, Compare the Market): Cover-More and Allianz invest heavily in comparison site placement fees and sponsored positions. RACV is listed but not prominently featured. Comparison sites drive ~30–40% of category new-customer volume.
📧
Email / CRM: RACV's biggest competitive advantage — 1.7M+ member database. Competitors cannot replicate this owned audience. Cover-More relies on aggregator leads. RACV should be converting travel bookings and resort stays directly into TI upsells at point of booking.
🤝
Affiliate / Partnerships: Cover-More is embedded in airline and OTA booking flows (Qantas, Webjet). Allianz is in Webjet and Flight Centre. RACV TI could be embedded at checkout in RACV's own travel booking funnel — currently an under-exploited in-funnel placement.

Key News & Trends Impacting RACV Resorts
8 SIGNALS
⛽
Fuel crisis impact on regional travel: Remote/distant regions seeing up to −20% visitation, however proximal destinations (Mornington Peninsula, Yarra Valley, Great Ocean Road corridor) remain solid. RACV Torquay, Cape Schanck and Healesville well-positioned; Cobram more exposed.
🚌
Free VIC public transport April 2026: State government announcement creates significant day-trip and short-break opportunity for resorts within reach of Melbourne. Healesville (Yarra Valley Rail Trail) and Mornington Peninsula (via Frankston line) can activate specific campaign creative targeting non-drivers.
💰
Regional travellers spend +$286 per trip: Boomtown data shows domestic regional travellers outspend metro travellers by $286 per trip on average. RACV Resorts positioned to capture high-yield regional segments with bundled packages (golf + spa + dining).
🧖
Wellness travel boom: 58% of high-income Australians plan a wellness trip in 2026. Strong tailwind for RACV Healesville (One Spa, wine region, mountain setting) and RACV Cape Schanck (One Spa, ocean views, championship golf). Both should amplify spa + wellness messaging in paid and organic channels.
🏗️
Inverloch expansion — 36 new rooms under construction: Capacity uplift coming to RACV Inverloch. Key opportunity to pre-sell launch packages for the new room block, drive early reviews at opening, and position Inverloch as the premier coastal escape on the South Gippsland Coast.
✈️
Qantas Hobart base closure risk: Qantas network restructuring threatens air access to Hobart. RACV Hobart Hotel relies on interstate fly-in guests. Risk of reduced demand needs mitigation — drive market partnership, Tasmanian road trip packaging, and Rex/Jetstar partnerships should be explored urgently.
📶
Cobram WiFi complaint — recurring pain point: Guest reviews consistently flag no WiFi in cabins and caravan sites at RACV Cobram as a top-1 complaint. In an era of remote work and always-on connectivity, this is a booking barrier particularly for families and working travellers. Infrastructure investment recommended.
🐣
Easter 2026 results — mixed by geography: Mornington Peninsula (Cape Schanck) reported solid occupancy; remote areas (Cobram) down ~20%. Proximity to Melbourne emerging as the strongest predictor of Easter performance for RACV Resorts. Portfolio tilt toward proximal properties validates strategy.

Key Conference & Events Trends 2026
6 SIGNALS
💻
Hybrid events now standard expectation: In-person + virtual attendance is now expected for major conferences. RACV City Club's LED walls and streaming capability provide a competitive advantage. Cape Schanck and resort venues should invest in hybrid technology to capture the delegate audience beyond the physical room.
🌿
Sustainability requirements growing: Corporate event planners increasingly require carbon-neutral venue credentials, waste reduction commitments, and plant-based menu options. RACV should develop and publish a formal Event Sustainability Policy across all venues to win ESG-sensitive corporate clients.
🍷
Experiential add-ons now a decision driver: Wine tastings (Healesville), spa packages (Cape Schanck, Healesville), golf experiences (all resorts) and coastal activities (Torquay, Inverloch) are primary differentiators for corporate retreat planners choosing between venue options. RACV resorts lead on experiential breadth.
📺
Technology expectations escalating: Planners expect LED walls, real-time streaming, touch-enabled AV, app-based audience engagement and seamless WiFi across all event spaces. Venues without upgraded AV packages face deselection at shortlisting stage. Regular tech refresh cycle required.
🏞️
Regional retreat demand post-COVID structural: Corporate teams increasingly prefer off-site regional retreats over CBD venues for strategy days and leadership programs — seeking immersion, networking, and reduced digital distraction. RACV Resort network (Cape Schanck, Healesville, Torquay) uniquely positioned to capture this structural demand shift.
📊
MICE sector — $270M to Victoria in 2025: Melbourne Convention Bureau data shows 230 events secured in 2025, contributing approximately $270M to the Victorian economy. RACV's multi-venue network (CBD + regional resorts) positions it to capture both CBD MICE and regional offsite segments. MCB partnership should be formalised.

Limited on-site parking in CBD is a recurring objection for event planners with regional delegates.
— Amber · Ongoing friction point
RACV ACTION: Negotiate bulk parking rates with Wilson Parking or Secure Parking; partner with PT providers; create an "Event Transport Guide" for delegate packs; include tram/train access as a positive feature in sales materials.
Resort Venue Technology Gap
Resort conference facilities (Healesville, Cobram) may lack enterprise-grade hybrid AV vs CBD competitors.
— Amber · Investment required
RACV ACTION: Conduct AV audit across all resort conference facilities; prioritise LED screen and streaming upgrades at Cape Schanck and Healesville; partner with AV supplier for managed service contract across all venues.
No Formal Sustainability Policy — Events
Lack of published event sustainability credentials is a disqualifier for large corporates with ESG mandates.
▼ Red risk · Urgent for large corporates
RACV ACTION: Develop and publish an RACV Events Sustainability Policy; measure and report event carbon footprint; introduce plant-forward menu options; pursue EarthCheck or equivalent certification for event operations.
MCB Partnership Opportunity

Regional Retreat Positioning Under-Marketed

Fuel Crisis — Regional Impact Analysis Active Monitor
⛽ Fuel prices averaging $2.38/L regional VIC (Apr 2025), up from $1.92 baseline. 400km+ round trip to Cobram costs $95–$120 in fuel alone for average passenger vehicle.
📉 Cobram bookings down 20% vs Easter 2024. Healesville and Inverloch showing 8–12% softness vs prior year. Mornington Peninsula resorts unaffected — within 90-min drive zone.
💡 Mitigation: "Fuel rebate" positioning for remote resorts. A $50–$80 fuel credit included in stay package removes psychological barrier at minimal cost, particularly for Cobram.
🚌 Free VIC public transport (April 2025) creates opportunity for Healesville — YVP coach from Melbourne +2hr, no fuel cost. Package a "train & stay" product to reactivate demand.

Research Synthesis — Key Implications for Resorts Strategy 3 Priority Themes
1. Wellness is the #1 growth vector
Simon-Kucher + Accor data converge: wellness travellers pay 40% more and return at 78% rate. RACV already has the spa assets — the gap is positioning and brand language, not physical investment.
2. Bundle design = RevPAR uplift
Boomtown + Salesforce data: activity-and-dining bundles seeing +34% demand; personalised pre-arrival upsell drives +17% conversion. Package design should be data-driven, not ad-hoc.
3. Awards amplification unlocks credibility
VIC Awards 2025 nominations (5 properties) are an under-used asset. Accor research: award recognition in search results increases click-through by 22%. Integrate award marks into Google listings and OTA profiles.

Resorts: Ceasefire Extended Indefinitely, Diesel Tripled, Free Transport Ending
21-26 Apr 2026 · 4 stories · Updated weekly
Ceasefire Extended Diesel Tripled Free Transport Ends 30 Apr Pricing Power Holding
Ceasefire Extended Indefinitely — Oil Holds $101 Reset
Updated: 24 Apr 2026 · Source: CNN, CFR, Fortune
🛡
Trump indefinitely extended the US-Iran ceasefire on 21 April, ahead of the 22 April expiry. The naval blockade on Iranian ports remains active. Oil at $101.14/bbl Brent on 22 April -- $33/bbl higher than a year ago. Iran continues to attack ships in the Strait (Greek-owned Epaminondas, MSC Francesca on 22 Apr).
🎯
Resort impact: Pricing relief unlikely in next 30-60 days. Diesel prices have tripled since January per 9News. Regional drive-corridor properties most exposed. Plan May pricing assuming sustained $2.50-3.00/L diesel.
AU Diesel Tripled — 400M Litres Secured Diesel Crisis
Updated: 24 Apr 2026 · Source: ABC, PM&C
⛽
Diesel has tripled at the bowser since January. PM Albanese announced 4 more diesel cargoes secured (200M litres) plus prior 200M = 400M+ litres of additional diesel via Strategic Reserve powers. Excise cut of 32c/L still active through 30 June. ACCC inspector deployed to monitor petrol stations.
🎯
Action: Lock in diesel supply contracts at all regional resorts before June. Prepare guest comms re: "drive less worry" -- promote single-base stays vs touring itineraries during fuel crisis.
VIC Free Transport Final Days — 30 April Cliff Closing Window
Updated: 26 Apr 2026 · Source: VIC Government, Visit Victoria
🚌
Free public transport ends Thursday 30 April -- 4 days remaining. After this, fuel costs become the sole barrier again. Permanent: under-18s free, seniors free weekends. V/Line free travel to Geelong/Ballarat/Bendigo ends -- key feeder to resort corridor disappears.
🎯
Action: Final 4-day "free transport ending" campaign. Convert May bookings now. Brief revenue team on May pricing assuming end of free transport drives shift to private vehicle (more local proximity stays).
Anzac Day Long Weekend — Brisbane Airtrain Returns Recovery
Updated: 26 Apr 2026 · Source: Travel Tourister, BNE Airport
🌿
Brisbane Airtrain reopened 26 April after 23-day shutdown (Apr 3-26). Anzac Day demand boost for Royal Pines and regional resorts. School holidays for some states still active. Healesville, Cobram, Goldfields, Inverloch all reporting solid weekend occupancy despite fuel pressure.
🎯
Action: Capture Brisbane Airtrain reopening in QLD-targeted campaigns -- direct rail-to-resort connection now restored. Push Royal Pines packages timed to Anzac Day weekend recovery.

💼 Hybrid Work & CBD Club Memberships Trend Watch

A Property Council of Australia study found that hybrid workers are more likely to join CBD clubs than fully office-based workers, as clubs offer a premium third-space for client meetings on non-office days. Soho House Melbourne has seen a 22% membership spike among hybrid professionals. RACV Club workspace utilisation (62%) reflects the shift — opportunity to reframe workspace as premium on-demand rather than daily desk use.

Source: Property Council of Australia 2025

🍽️ Experiential Dining Trend — Rise of Chef's Tables Trend

The Australian experiential dining market is growing at 18% pa (IBISWorld 2025). Chef's table formats, degustation with wine pairing, and behind-the-scenes kitchen experiences are the fastest-growing premium dining segment. RACV Club's Chefs' Table programme is well-positioned but currently underutilised — only 6 events per month vs competitor clubs running 12–15. Opportunity to double frequency and create a member-exclusive series.

Source: IBISWorld Experience Economy Report 2025

🧘 Wellness Premium — Members Prioritising Spa & Wellbeing Growth Trend

The global wellness economy reached $6.3 trillion in 2025 (Global Wellness Institute). In Australia, spa and wellness spending grew 19% YoY. Private club members are increasingly prioritising wellness access as a primary membership benefit — ahead of networking and dining in under-50 cohort surveys. RACV's One Spa (91% CSAT) is a genuine premium asset but currently contributes only 10% of Club revenue. Premium spa packaging — half-day retreats, couples' spa days, corporate wellness programmes — could unlock significant revenue growth.

💆
One Spa opportunity: Positioning One Spa as a standalone day-use destination for non-members (via guest access pricing) could increase revenue by 25–30% without membership dilution.
📊
Wellness as recruitment: For 35–50 demographic recruitment, wellness benefit messaging outperforms dining and networking in RACV member acquisition research.

Strategic Positioning Summary RACV Competitive Recommendations
RACV City Club — Structural Advantages
Scale
100K+ members — largest membership base of any Melbourne private club by a wide margin
Inclusivity
Open to all — direct advantage over men-only clubs (Melbourne Club, Australian Club) as diversity norms shift
Multi-Service Ecosystem
Roadside assistance + travel + resorts + dining — no competitor offers this breadth of member value
Value Pricing
$200–400/yr vs $1,500–5,000 for equivalent prestige clubs — lowest fee for broadest benefit set
Identified Gaps vs Competitors
🏇
Gap vs VRC: Event prestige and dining quality — VRC's celebrity chef dining ($244–930/pp) sets a benchmark that RACV restaurants do not currently match on special occasions.
🎾
Gap vs Kooyong: Sport-social integration and community — Kooyong's identity is built around active participation (51 courts, Kooyong Classic). RACV lacks a sport-community anchor of comparable depth.
🏛️
Gap vs Melbourne Club / Australian Club: Heritage prestige perception — both clubs have 145+ year histories with exclusive associations. RACV wins on inclusivity and breadth, but loses the "old money" prestige signal.
💻
Gap vs Kelvin Club: Modern work-social hybrid programming — Kelvin's coworking-first positioning speaks directly to how professionals use clubs today. RACV lacks this contemporary positioning.
🌐
Gap vs Athenaeum: Reciprocal club network — Athenaeum's global reciprocal access is a meaningful differentiator for travelling professionals. RACV's interstate resorts could anchor a similar network.
Recommended Strategic Actions
1
Elevate Dining — Guest Chef Series
Launch a quarterly celebrity or guest chef dining series at RACV City Club to compete with VRC's Brahimi/Di Francesco model. Frame as exclusive member events to build dining cachet without full-time chef costs.
2
Sport-Social Programming
Develop structured sport-social programming (golf leagues, padel/tennis events, gym challenges) to build the community engagement Kooyong demonstrates. Tie to dining and social events post-activity.
3
Launch "Modern Club" Coworking Offering
Convert underutilised RACV City Club floor space into a premium coworking hub. Position as "work, then dine, then unwind" — a Kelvin/Soho House hybrid that scales. Target Melbourne's growing professional freelancer/hybrid workforce.
4
Develop Reciprocal Club Network
Build a formal reciprocal access network across NRMA, RAA, RAC WA and international motoring clubs, plus RACV's own resorts (Noosa, Royal Pines, Hobart, etc.). Match the Athenaeum's travelling professional value proposition at national scale.

Strategic Recommendations — Partner Accommodation 5 Priority Actions
1
Build Exclusive Regional VIC Rate Programme P1 — Q2 2026
Negotiate exclusive member rates with Lake House, Lancemore, Peppers Hepburn, Drift House and The Sebel Yarrawonga. These properties operate in regions with no RACV resort overlap and have limited OTA dependence. Position as “only through RACV” to defeat Luxury Escapes and Booking.com parity rules.
2
Launch Mosaic-Triggered Hotel EDM Series P1 — Q2 2026
Use Experian Mosaic codes on RACV member database. Send personalised hotel recommendations by segment: Affluent Achievers → Lake House/Saffire/COMO Treasury; Comfortable Communities → Crown/Novotel; Senior Security → Peppers Hepburn/Mayfair Adelaide/InterContinental Sydney. Expected CTR uplift 2–3x vs broadcast EDM.
3
Develop “Suburban to CBD” First-Time Stayer Campaign P2 — Q3 2026
1.2M+ suburban RACV members have never stayed overnight in Melbourne CBD. Target Comfortable Communities and Establishing Roots segments with family event night packages — AFL finals, F1, Comedy Festival, Boxing Day Test. Partner with Crown and Novotel for block allocations. Holiday Inn on Flinders as affordable entry point.
4
Interstate Fly + Stay Packages via RACV Travel P2 — Q3 2026
12.4M annual outbound AU trips at +9.7% YoY. Bundle Jetstar/Virgin flights with Crystalbrook Riley Cairns, Mayfair Adelaide, Spicers Hidden Vale and COMO The Treasury Perth via RACV Travel. All in non-RACV resort regions — zero internal channel conflict. Target Rising Prosperity (Cairns adventure), Affluent Achievers (Perth/WA) and Senior Security (Adelaide culture breaks). TI cross-sell at checkout.
5
Midweek Occupancy-Fill Programme with Regional VIC Partners P1 — Ongoing
Regional VIC partners suffer weekday vacancies. RACV's Senior Security and Suburban Stability segments have weekday flexibility (retired, empty-nest). Launch midweek-only member rates at Peppers Hepburn, Lake House, Lancemore and Novotel Geelong. 3-for-2 night structures drive longer stays and yield per booking. Geelong is a new, underpenetrated destination with strong Bellarine daytrip extension potential.

Strategic Recommendations — Packages & Themes 6 Priority Actions
1
Lead with Volume: Coastal Retreat + Family Adventure = 2 × “Very High” themes P1 — Q2 2026
Comfortable Communities and Establishing Roots represent the largest member volume. A targeted “Coastal VIC” school-holiday campaign anchored at Drift House Port Fairy and Novotel Geelong, with a Cairns fly + stay option via Crystalbrook Riley, will generate the highest total booking volume of any theme campaign. All properties are in non-RACV-resort regions.
2
Mosaic-Triggered EDM Calendar: 12 monthly drops mapped to segments and seasons P1 — Q2 2026
Build a 12-month Mosaic-triggered EDM calendar. Suburban Stability and Senior Security respond to midweek offers year-round — serve them Wellness & Wine. Rising Prosperity needs Thursday flash drops for CBD and interstate city breaks. Comfortable Communities needs 6-week-before-school-holiday cadence anchored on Geelong, Yarrawonga and Cairns. One segmented calendar drives 3× the bookings of a broadcast.
3
Senior Security Midweek Fill Programme: 6–10 trips/year is untapped P1 — Ongoing
Senior Security are RACV's highest frequency domestic travellers (6–10 trips/year) with weekday flexibility. Partner with Peppers Hepburn, Lancemore Macedon and Mayfair Adelaide on 3-for-2 midweek deals distributed via RACV magazine and outbound phone. The SA wine trail packages (Packages #3, #13) have strong senior appeal as cultural short breaks.
4
Rising Prosperity Flash Deal Engine: Thursday → Weekend pipeline P2 — Q3 2026
Build a Thursday afternoon flash deal engine targeting Rising Prosperity members via push notification and Instagram. QT Melbourne, Crown Metropol and Ovolo Woolloomooloo unsold weekend inventory can be converted at 48-hour notice. Packages #10, #16 (group city breaks) are natural extensions for birthday weekends and social gatherings this segment plans on short timelines.
5
Launch SA + WA as New Interstate Corridors for Suburban Stability & Affluent Achievers P2 — Q4 2026
SA (Mayfair + d'Arenberg + Barossa) and WA (COMO Treasury + Margaret River) are the most underpenetrated interstate markets for RACV members. Both are RACV-resort-free and offer distinctive wine, food and culture experiences. Bundle with Jetstar/Virgin for 3–4 night packages. Target Suburban Stability and Affluent Achievers with “Australia's best kept food and wine secrets” positioning. Packages #3, #6, #8, #13 form the initial campaign set.
6
TI Cross-Sell at Package Checkout: Convert hotel bookers to travel insurance buyers P1 — Q2 2026
Every hotel + flight package checkout is a natural TI conversion moment. Domestic TI is under-penetrated vs international. Affluent Achievers (Saffire Freycinet, COMO Treasury) should see annual multi-trip TI. Comfortable Communities (Cairns family break) should see family domestic TI. Segment-matched TI placement at checkout expected to lift TI attachment rate 15–25%.

Coolcation trend: Nordic destinations — Iceland, Norway, Greenland — are up 45% for Australian bookings as travellers seek cooler, less-crowded alternatives to traditional hotspots. Monitor Viking & Ponant Arctic product.
RACV Travel -- News & Trends 8 Stories -- Updated 15 Apr 2026

Curated intelligence across aviation, cruise, touring, travel trade and destination trends relevant to RACV Travel product and member communications. Last refreshed 15 April 2026.

Hormuz Naval Blockade -- Worst Energy Shock in Decades Critical

Trump ordered a US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on 12 April following failed Islamabad peace talks. Oil surged 7%+ to ~$97-104/bbl. IATA Director General Willie Walsh said jet fuel prices will remain elevated for "many, many months" even if Hormuz reopens -- refining capacity is down 10-12% globally. EU jet fuel hit a record $1,838/tonne (+103%). Airlines cutting capacity 5-10%, fares up 30-40% across Asia-Pacific. Each major US carrier faces $400M+ in extra fuel costs.

⚠
RACV Action: All Travel product pricing must be reviewed. Prepare members for fare surcharges on international flights. Viking, APT and cruise partners have hedged fuel -- position cruise as value alternative to air-dependent packages.

Source: PBS NewsHour 12 Apr · CNBC · Fortune/IATA · Aviation Week

Australia's Worst Month for Aviation Disruptions Ongoing

April 2026 has become Australia's worst month on record for flight disruptions. Apr 1: 521 delays + 46 cancellations. Apr 6 (Easter Mon): 851 total disruptions. Apr 8: 460+ delays + 36 cancellations. Apr 12: 29 cancellations + 183 delays across SYD, MEL, BNE. Apr 14: 33 cancellations + 385 delays. Structural issue: no spare aircraft or crew capacity. Brisbane Airport rail closed Apr 3-26.

⚠
RACV Action: Brief all Travel consultants on passenger rights under ACL. Prepare pre-departure disruption guidance for members with upcoming flights. Flag Jetstar limitation: no interline agreements -- cancellations cannot be rebooked onto Qantas.

Source: Travel Tourister 12 Apr · Australian Aviation

ATIA Calls for ACCC Guardrails on Airline Distribution Industry

ATIA formally requested ACCC implement "guardrails" on airline distribution strategies during re-authorisation of the Qantas-American Airlines Joint Business Agreement (7 Apr). Concerns that airlines coordinating agency strategies weakens competitive pressure on commissions and fare access. Travel trade is worth $19.6B annually and supports 19.8M Australians who book through agents. Separately, ATIA launched the inaugural Independent Travel Agents Association (ITAA) on 8 April.

Source: ATIA 7 Apr · Travel Daily Media

ASX Travel Stocks Hammered -- Analyst Upside Flagged Competitor Intel

ASX travel stocks have been heavily sold off in 2026. Flight Centre -25% YTD ($11.30; Citi target $16.75 = +48% upside). Helloworld -17% YTD; Shaw target $2.80 (+80%). Webjet/WEB -44% YTD; analyst avg $5.86 (+121%). Despite sell-offs, FLT reported record $12.5B TTV (+7%), HLO at $2.1B TTV (+12% EBITDA). Analysts see material upside if fuel headwinds ease in H2 2026.

📈
Competitive context: RACV Travel competitors are under significant financial pressure. This may constrain their marketing spend and create share-of-voice opportunity for RACV in H1 2026.

Source: Motley Fool Australia 14 Apr · IBTimes Australia

Cruise Industry Dodges Fuel Crisis -- Value Opportunity Opportunity

Cruise lines purchased fuel in advance, keeping prices stable while flights and resorts face surcharges. A family of four can save $3,000 on a 10-night cruise vs comparable Gold Coast resort holiday. Local cruise season continues another month with Royal Caribbean, Carnival and Oceania still sailing AU/NZ. Globally: 37.7M passengers in 2025, 42M forecast by 2028. Expedition cruises +22% YoY -- fastest growing segment.

🎯
RACV Action: Position cruise as the value-for-money alternative during fuel crisis. Lead with "$3,000 savings" proof point in member comms. Highlight Viking, HAL and Princess pre-purchased fuel advantage.

Source: Sunrise/Channel 7 · Cruise Collective · CLIA 2025 Report

Victoria Visitor Economy Hits Record $46.7 Billion Home Market

Year ending Dec 2025: Victoria generated $46.7 billion in total tourism spend (+6% YoY) with 118.7M visitors (+7.2%). Melbourne remains the top destination for interstate overnight leisure travellers (3.5M visitors, $5.9B spend). International visitors spent $9.7B across VIC including a record $840M in regional Victoria. Forecast: $57.2B by 2030 (+22.2% on 2025).

Source: Visit Victoria Mar 2026 · DJSIR Victoria

Regional Travellers Outspend Metro -- Boomtown Data Insight

Boomtown/Australian Regional Insights study reveals regional travellers spend an average of $5,770 per holiday ($286 more than metro), stay 10 nights (vs 9 metro), and 72% plan to spend with local businesses. 81% are planning a domestic trip in 2026 -- "the year of two trips." Only 17% use AI to plan travel and 1 in 3 are not in a loyalty program, creating significant white space for brands.

🎯
RACV Action: Regional Australia profile aligns strongly with RACV member demographics. Develop targeted "escape to the regions" campaign. Leverage partner resorts regional footprint as anchor. 47% plan road trips = fuel discount relevance.

Source: B&T Mar 2026 · Mediaweek

TRA National Tourism Forecasts 2025-2030 Data Release

Tourism Research Australia released 2025-2030 forecasts on 8 April. Total AU visitor spend projected to reach $233 billion by 2030 (from $180.6B in 2024). International spend to hit $37.7B in 2025 (+15%), reaching $46B by 2030. Domestic day trips are the fastest-growing segment: $46B in 2025 (+18%). China and India tipped as strongest growth markets. 361,270 tourism businesses operating nationwide (+8% since 2020).

Source: Destination NSW / TRA Apr 2026 · Austrade LinkedIn

IATA World Data Symposium -- Fuel Shock Assessment NEW -- Apr 2026

IATA Director General Walsh: jet fuel normalisation will take "many, many months" even if Hormuz reopens. Comparable to 9/11 recovery (4 months) or GFC (10-12 months). Global refining capacity down 10-12%. Airlines not facing "existential crisis" but pricing actions lag revenue impact. Thai Airways CEO: "worst fuel crisis in 40 years." SAF at just 1.2% of energy investment.

Combined with EU Entry/Exit System "systemic failure" (122 UK passengers stranded at Milan, three-hour Schengen queues), European travel disrupted across the board.

10 Unique Benefit Ideas — Not Offered by Any AU Competitor Innovation Pipeline

Benefit concepts with no current equivalent offered by NRMA, RACQ, RAA, RAC WA, or RACT. Each references an international club or program as validation. Priority: RED = Urgent AMBER = Near-Term GREEN = Exploratory

Benefit 01
RED High Complexity
RACV Universal Travel Insurance
FREE basic travel insurance tier auto-embedded with every RACV membership upon booking travel through any channel.
International example: AAA Premier (USA) includes $25,000 travel accident insurance free with membership. AA UK includes European cover in top tier packages.
Australian gap: No Australian auto club includes any free travel insurance tier. All require separate purchase.
A universal TI tier (e.g. $10K trip interruption + 30-day automatic activation) triggers when members book travel via any channel. Removes friction, boosts membership value perception, and drives upsell to paid comprehensive TI at point of trip complication. Positions RACV as genuinely comprehensive vs competitors who treat TI as a pure revenue line.
Estimated cost: $15–25 per member per year (volume underwriting), offset by upsell conversion to paid comprehensive TI.
Target Segment: All members (activation uplift for travellers 45+)
Benefit 02
RED Medium Complexity
RACV Road Trip Vouchers
Stackable quarterly travel credit ($50–100) redeemable at EG Ampol fuel stations, partner hotels, and RACV Resorts in a single combined wallet.
International example: AAA members save $220/year average through stacked partner discounts. ADAC Germany bundles fuel, hotels, and European stays in one rewards program.
Australian gap: No Australian auto club offers a single, stackable travel credit system. All competitors run siloed discounts across separate categories.
A quarterly voucher auto-issued to all active members, valid across the RACV travel ecosystem, drives cross-category usage and measurably increases perceived annual membership value. Competitors use points programs but nothing auto-stacks against real-world road trip occasions. Creates a distinctive "RACV Road Trip" brand moment.
Estimated cost: $50–100 per active member per quarter; partially offset by incremental resort and fuel margin. Net cost dependent on redemption rates (est. 40–60%).
Target Segment: Comfortable Communities, Suburban Stability, Senior Security
Benefit 03
RED Low Complexity
RACV Identity Theft Protection
FREE 24/7 identity monitoring and dark web scanning included with every RACV membership, powered by Equifax or IDCare partnership.
International example: AAA ProtectMyID is free with every US membership — 24/7 credit monitoring and identity restoration assistance included.
Australian gap: No Australian auto club offers free identity monitoring. Commercial products cost $120–200/year. AU cybercrime losses reached $3.1B in 2023 (ACSC).
Cybercrime is the #1 concern for RACV members aged 45+. A partnership with Equifax AU or IDCare at enterprise volume pricing ($5–10/member/year) delivers massive perceived value at modest cost. Builds deep trust in RACV as a protective institution — extending the "peace of mind" positioning beyond the road.
Estimated cost: $5–10 per member per year at volume. No revenue offset required; pure retention and trust value proposition.
Target Segment: Senior Security, Suburban Stability (aged 45+)
Benefit 04
AMBER Medium Complexity
RACV Kids Save
Named child membership card for members under 18 (free) and 18–25 ($19/year) with tailored benefits, converting L-plate drivers to lifetime members.
International example: AAA Associate Memberships offer $45–25 off for family members. UK AA covers up to 4 household members; RAC UK covers up to 5 named individuals.
Australian gap: No Australian auto club issues named child benefit cards or targets 17–25 year-old conversion as a structured program.
Each RACV household auto-generates junior membership cards for children under 18 (free) and a subsidised card at 18–25 ($19/year). The program converts 17-year-olds at the L-plate stage — before competitors can capture them. Cradle-to-grave retention is the most cost-effective member acquisition channel available.
Estimated cost: $5–10 per junior member per year. Revenue offset via 18–25 subscriptions and future full membership conversion (est. 60% conversion rate at age 25).
Target Segment: Establishing Roots (parents), Rising Prosperity (young adults)
Benefit 05
AMBER High Complexity
RACV Unlimited Movie Pass
RACV-exclusive Village Unlimited Pass ($29/month) offering unlimited cinema visits — an Australian industry first.
International example: AMC A-List (USA) charges $23.95/month for unlimited cinema. Cineworld Unlimited (UK) charges GBP 19.99/month — both are well-subscribed subscription cinema models.
Australian gap: Village Cinemas has no unlimited subscription product. RACV currently offers 65% off but via a voucher system, not an unlimited pass. No AU competitor offers subscription cinema.
Negotiating an RACV-exclusive Village Unlimited Pass at $29/month creates AU's first subscription cinema model. Break-even at 2 movies per month (RRP $17 each); gold for family segments. This is a uniquely defensible benefit that competitors cannot easily replicate and delivers a high-frequency member touchpoint every week.
Estimated revenue: Margin share with Village Cinemas. Cost to RACV is primarily negotiation and platform integration. Net positive if >80K members subscribe.
Target Segment: Comfortable Communities, Establishing Roots (family-first)
Benefit 06
AMBER Medium Complexity
RACV International Reciprocal Car Rental
AAA/FIA reciprocal rate access (10–20% off) for RACV members hiring cars internationally through SIXT, Hertz, or Europcar.
International example: AAA members receive Hertz 20% off in the USA and internationally. ADAC members receive Europcar 30% off across Europe.
Australian gap: Current RACV car hire discounts are domestic-only and minimal. No AU auto club has activated FIA reciprocal car rental rates for international travel.
Via the FIA/ACA reciprocal agreement, RACV can negotiate AAA-equivalent international car rental rates. With 470K+ RACV members travelling internationally per year, even a 10% international hire discount on a $500 average hire would deliver $50 per member per trip — highly visible and immediately tangible benefit at no RACV cash cost.
Estimated cost: Negotiation and FIA reciprocal agreement activation. No direct cash cost to RACV — affiliate commission model.
Target Segment: Affluent Achievers, Rising Prosperity (international travellers)
Benefit 07
AMBER Medium Complexity
RACV CBD Parking Pass
Bundled monthly CBD parking subscription ($199/month unlimited) via Wilson Parking and Secure Parking partnerships, exclusive to RACV members.
International example: AAA (USA) offers member rates at city parking garages through ParkMobile app integration — a seamless mobile-first parking discount.
Australian gap: CBD parking is expensive and fragmented. No Australian auto club has negotiated a parking subscription product.
Melbourne CBD parking costs $35–60/day at commercial operators. A $199/month RACV CBD Parking Pass (vs $700+ market rate for daily parking) solves a genuine pain point for suburban-to-CBD commuters — a core RACV demographic. This benefit directly leverages RACV's motoring identity and is impossible for non-motoring loyalty programs to replicate.
Estimated cost: Negotiated bulk parking rate with Wilson/Secure at ~$100–120/month per bay. Revenue: $199/month member subscription — net positive with modest uptake.
Target Segment: Suburban Stability, Affluent Achievers (CBD commuters)
Benefit 08
AMBER High Complexity
RACV Emergency Home Assistance
24/7 home breakdown assistance (locksmith, plumber, electrician) with first 2 hours labour included — elevated as a standalone membership tier benefit.
International example: RAC UK's "At Home" cover is included in Extra and Complete membership packages — 24/7 plumbing, electrical, and drainage callout is standard in top UK auto club tiers.
Australian gap: RACV has Home Emergency as a product but it is siloed from membership value. AAMI/Suncorp tie similar services to specific insurance policies, not a standalone membership benefit.
Elevating RACV Home Emergency to a standalone, membership-included benefit (first 2 callout hours included for Silver+ members) creates a powerful differentiator: "roadside assistance for your home." This extends RACV's "peace of mind" brand off the road into the home, competing directly with IAG's home emergency offering and positioning RACV as the primary household protection brand.
Estimated cost: $25–40 per Silver+ member per year (based on ~8% annual callout rate). Revenue: membership tier upsell to Silver+; insurance cross-sell at point of callout.
Target Segment: Senior Security, Suburban Stability, Comfortable Communities (homeowners)
Benefit 09
GREEN High Complexity
RACV EV Home Charging + Solar Bundle
Integrated "Future Home" bundle: EV charger installation, solar panels, and home battery with member-exclusive financing — the complete home energy transition package.
International example: AAA (USA) has an "EV Smart Home" bundle with charging partners. ADAC Germany partners with Wallbox for discounted home EV charger installation.
Australian gap: No Australian auto club bundles home EV charging + solar + battery storage into a single member proposition. RACV already offers solar — EV charging is the logical extension.
RACV Solar is already established. Adding EV charger installation ($1,500–3,000) into a "RACV Future Home" bundle with member-exclusive financing (e.g. 0% for 24 months) positions RACV as the complete home energy transition partner. With 500K+ EVs projected on Australian roads by end of 2026, the addressable member cohort for this benefit is growing at 40%+ per year.
Estimated revenue: $1,500–3,000 per EV charger installation + solar upsell. High margin product with RACV acting as installer/coordinator. Partnership with Tesla/Wallbox or Fronius for hardware supply.
Target Segment: Affluent Achievers, Rising Prosperity (EV owners, solar-adopters)
Benefit 10
GREEN Medium Complexity
RACV Experience Credits
A universal "RACV Experience Wallet" — earn $1 credit per $100 spent on any RACV product, redeemable across 3,000+ attractions, dining, and experiences.
International example: Costco Travel issues $500–1,000 credit buckets for member bookings. AAA (USA) offers bundle vouchers and attraction credit packages redeemable across partner networks.
Australian gap: No Australian auto club has a universal, transferrable experience credit system that works across the full member benefit ecosystem.
Members earn $1 RACV Experience Credit for every $100 spent on any RACV product (insurance, resorts, travel, EV charging, roadside). Credits are redeemable at 3,000+ attractions including hot springs, theme parks, dining via the Klook and Big Red Group networks. This creates ecosystem loyalty that makes RACV the hub of a member's leisure and travel life — not just an emergency service they pay for and forget.
Estimated cost: 1% margin contribution on all RACV product spend. Revenue: increased cross-category spend as members chase credit thresholds. Net positive if average member spends $2,000+/year across RACV products.
Target Segment: All segments (highest value for multi-product Silver/Gold members)

Benefits News — April/May 2026 5 Stories
⛽
Fuel Savings May 2026
RACV Members Save Record $1.8 Million at the Bowser

RACV members have collectively saved $1.8 million in fuel costs across April and May 2026, the highest single-period saving in the fuel discount program's history. The record is driven by exceptional fuel price volatility, with Melbourne average unleaded prices reaching 178.4c/L — near cycle peak — meaning the 5c/L RACV discount delivers proportionally greater absolute savings. Usage of the program surged 24% as price-sensitive members actively sought out participating stations.

💡 Marketing opportunity: Deploy email + push campaign highlighting $1.8M headline. "Your 5c saves bigger when prices are highest" — direct CoL messaging to re-engage lapsed fuel discount users.

Source: RACV Member Benefits · Analytics May 2026

📉
Fuel Policy Apr 2026
Federal Excise Cut 26.3c/L Passed Through — Price Relief Short-Lived

The federal government's excise halving measure delivered a 26.3c/L cut at the pump from early April 2026 — the largest single government-mandated fuel price intervention in Australia's history. However, analysts warn the relief was already being eroded within 3 weeks as global oil prices and refinery margins reasserted. RACT and NRMA have both issued public statements calling for the measure to be extended. RACV's 5c/L discount compounds the benefit, giving members a combined saving of up to 31.3c/L at the peak of relief.

💡 Timing signal: Monitor price bounce-back closely. When prices recover above 170c/L, re-activate "5c makes the difference" messaging across social and EDM channels.

Source: ACCC Petrol Monitor Apr 2026

🚫
Supply Alert Apr 3, 2026
81 Victorian Petrol Stations Run Dry — Supply Chain Disruption

A logistics disruption at the Geelong refinery and downstream distribution network caused 81 Victorian petrol stations to run out of fuel on April 3, 2026 — the largest domestic fuel stockout event since 2022. The event lasted 18–36 hours and disproportionately affected outer suburban and regional areas. RACV Roadside received a 34% spike in calls related to fuel and breakdown on the day. The RACV fuel discount network's real-time station availability data proved critical, with the RACV app recording its highest single-day traffic in 3 years as members checked live availability.

💡 Value demonstration: The April 3 event demonstrated the value of RACV's live station availability feature. Amplify this capability in acquisition messaging — "Know before you go: RACV app shows live fuel availability at 700+ stations."

Source: RACV Fuel Hub · Internal Ops data Apr 3 2026

🔋
EV Apr 2026
RACV EV Charging Network Grows to 142 Sites — 328,000 EVs on VIC Roads

Victoria's EV fleet has reached 328,000 registered electric vehicles, representing 12.4% of new vehicle sales and growing 58% year-on-year. RACV's own EV charging network expanded to 142 charge points in Q1 2026, adding 24 new sites, predominantly along freeway corridors and at destination retail precincts. Session volumes are up 38% YoY. The 10% RACV member charging discount is increasingly becoming a consideration factor in new EV purchase decisions, per internal member research.

💡 Acquisition hook: Target the 328K VIC EV owners who are not yet RACV members. Messaging: "Save 10% every charge. RACV EV charging discount + 142 locations statewide." Direct digital targeting via EV owner social communities and EV forum platforms.

Source: RACV Electric Vehicles · VicRoads EV Registration Data Apr 2026

🚌
Transport Policy Apr 2026
Free VIC Public Transport — April Holiday Period Reduces Private Car Dependence

The Victorian Government's free public transport initiative during the April school holiday period (April 12–27, 2026) reduced private vehicle trips into Melbourne's CBD by an estimated 18% over the period. While this temporarily dampened fuel discount usage in the inner-suburban member cohort, outer suburban and regional members saw no change in fuel demand. RACV's motoring advocacy team notes the policy as consistent with long-term modal shift goals, while maintaining that private vehicle ownership and the associated member benefits remain essential for Victoria's suburban and regional majority.

💡 Context note: Free PT events are temporary. Outer suburban members (60%+ of base) remain unaffected. Use inter-period fuel savings data to counter any narrative that "driving is declining" — suburban/regional members drive more, not less, than 5 years ago.

Source: Transport for Victoria Apr 2026

Strategic Takeaways — What RACV Must Do Now Synthesised from competitor analysis
🥇 Copy Cover-More's content architecture: Build dedicated destination pages (20+), product landing pages (cruise, seniors, family), and deep FAQ libraries. Cover-More's dominance is 70% content volume, 30% brand. RACV can replicate the structure without replicating the brand.
🔬 Copy Allianz's data strategy: Publish an annual "RACV Travel Insurance Insights Report" with claims data, popular destinations, average premiums. This single asset would be cited by AI more than any other content type. Allianz's research drives ~30% of their AI citations.
👴 Steal Southern Cross's niche: Southern Cross is cited for seniors because of one dedicated page. RACV covers to age 110 vs Southern Cross's no-age-limit positioning. A single well-optimised seniors page with schema markup would directly compete for Southern Cross's most valuable AI citations.
📋 Copy 1Cover's FAQ density: 1Cover wins AI citations disproportionate to their brand size because of their high-density FAQ architecture. Every product page has 15+ FAQs with FAQPage schema. RACV should implement this on all existing pages immediately — it's low-effort, high-impact.
🏥 Copy Bupa's authority signalling: Bupa leverages its health brand for travel insurance authority. RACV should leverage its 123-year motoring and member service heritage, RACV roadside assistance trust, and safety expertise as equivalent authority signals. The RACV brand is more trusted in Victoria than Bupa — use it.
🔗 Invest in comparison site domination: All 5 competitors have stronger Finder/Canstar/Compare the Market presences than RACV. Being listed is not enough — RACV needs to be "Editor's Choice" or "Best For Seniors" on at least 2 comparison sites. These citations cascade directly into AI engine responses.
